description: MICROARCHITECTURE — the sub-world of computer_architecture: how one processor realises its instruction set. Gives the concept-graph descent a third rung.

microtheory.name: microarchitecture
microtheory.definition: The concrete implementation of an instruction set in one processor: the pipeline stages, hazard handling, out-of-order and superscalar execution that turn the architectural contract into gates and clocks.

concepts.name: pipeline_stage
concepts.definition: One step (fetch, decode, execute, memory, writeback) of an instruction pipeline.

concepts.name: data_hazard
concepts.definition: A pipeline stall when an instruction needs a result not yet produced.

concepts.name: forwarding
concepts.definition: Bypassing a result directly to a dependent instruction to avoid a stall.

concepts.name: out_of_order_execution
concepts.definition: Executing instructions as operands become ready, not in program order.

concepts.name: superscalar
concepts.definition: Issuing more than one instruction per clock via duplicated execution units.

concepts.name: speculation
concepts.definition: Executing past an unresolved branch on a predicted path, squashing if wrong.

concepts.name: reorder_buffer
concepts.definition: The structure that retires out-of-order results back into program order.

concepts.name: register_renaming
concepts.definition: Mapping architectural registers to a larger physical set to remove false dependencies.

concepts.name: branch_prediction
concepts.definition: Guessing a branch outcome to keep the pipeline supplied with instructions.

concepts.name: instruction_retirement
concepts.definition: Committing a completed instruction's effects, in order, to architectural state.
